system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 2 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

[Image: four figures with various numbers of circles connected are shown.]

A sequence of four figures is shown above.

A. Complete the table below for Figure 4.

| Figure | Number of Circles |
| :---: | :---: |
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 3 |
| 3 | 5 |
| 4 | |

B. If there were a Figure 5, how many circles would it have?

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
A horizontal sequence of four figures composed of identical circles:
- Figure 1 consists of 1 circle, labeled "Figure 1" below.
- Figure 2 consists of 3 circles forming an inverted V-shape, with 1 circle at the top touching 1 circle to the lower left and 1 circle to the lower right, labeled "Figure 2" below.
- Figure 3 consists of 5 circles forming an inverted V-shape, with 1 circle at the apex, a branch of 2 circles extending downward and to the left, and a branch of 2 circles extending downward and to the right, labeled "Figure 3" below.
- Figure 4 consists of 7 circles forming an inverted V-shape, with 1 circle at the apex, a branch of 3 circles extending downward and to the left, and a branch of 3 circles extending downward and to the right, labeled "Figure 4" below.

## Question 2

[Image: four figures with various numbers of circles connected.]

A sequence of four figures is shown above.

C. If the figures were continued, how many circles would there be in Figure 10? (Do not draw the figures.)

Answer: ____

Figure, described in words:
Four figures labeled 'Figure 1', 'Figure 2', 'Figure 3', and 'Figure 4' are displayed from left to right:
- Figure 1 consists of a single circle.
- Figure 2 consists of 3 circles forming an arch or inverted V-shape: 1 circle at the top, with 1 circle touching its lower left and 1 circle touching its lower right.
- Figure 3 consists of 5 circles forming an arch: 1 circle at the apex, with 2 circles extending down to the left and 2 circles extending down to the right.
- Figure 4 consists of 7 circles forming an arch: 1 circle at the apex, with 3 circles extending down to the left and 3 circles extending down to the right.

Answer each of the 2 questions.

answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

output.answer_2:
C. Let's look at the pattern. Figure 1 has 1 circle, Figure 2 has 3 circles, Figure 3 has 5 circles, and Figure 4 has 7 circles. The number of circles increases by 2 each time. So:

Figure 1: 1
Figure 2: 3 (1 + 2)
Figure 3: 5 (3 + 2)
Figure 4: 7 (5 + 2)

Following this pattern:
Figure 5: 9 (7 + 2)
Figure 6: 11 (9 + 2)
Figure 7: 13 (11 + 2)
Figure 8: 15 (13 + 2)
Figure 9: 17 (15 + 2)
Figure 10: 19 (17 + 2)

So, Figure 10 would have 19 circles.
